text:
Florida arrives on a 4-1-0 run, most recently a 5-3 win over Chicago three days ago, and it opens a three-game road trip in Washington short-handed. Brad Marchand (knee) is on injured reserve and Anton Lundell is out, though ESPN's estimated return for Lundell is Nov 8. Carter Verhaeghe has taken Marchand's spot beside Sam Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk. Washington has lost two straight, including a 6-5 loss to Dallas in which Jason Robertson scored three goals. The Capitals are without Vincent Desharnais.

The numbers see little between them. At five on five, FLA has taken 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in its games and WSH 53%, and our model has it 3.21 to 3.29 tonight. The special-teams matchup to watch: FLA's power play creates 1.14 expected goals a game against a WSH penalty kill that allows 0.80, and Florida takes 5.2 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Akira Schmid (FLA) and Logan Thompson (WSH) are both at .888 or below in save percentage this season. Thompson is +1.2 goals saved above expected, Schmid +0.3, and Thompson was +28.2 last season.

Tkachuk has 16 points in his last ten games, and Reinhart has scored in four straight. Our model gives Reinhart a 39% chance to score. On the Washington side, Alex Tuch is the likeliest to score at 38%. Tom Wilson has no points in ten games despite 3.4 expected goals, so we'd call him due.
